quantities.about: The quantity vocabulary of the variable table. A variable may name one quantity; its dimension must agree with the unit and the dimension formula. Familiar groups (groups.json) match on these ids, never on symbols. temperature: absolute or difference. meaning: the physical meaning a dimensionless quantity keeps.

quantities.name: thermal contact resistance per unit area

groups.about: Familiar dimensionless groups, each stored as formulas over quantities with explicit reference quantities, never as a name alone (spec section 10). A group matches a calculated group when one of its forms gives the same exponent for each supplied variable through a one-to-one match of quantities. phase, kind and role narrow a term: phase fluid or solid; kind parameter (the default, which also matches a constant), field, coordinate or any. A recognized name is a proposed interpretation until the researcher confirms it. Order is the preference order for a familiar basis.

groups.label: Nu
groups.name: Nusselt number
groups.reference: L is the characteristic length of the declared geometry and k_f is the fluid conductivity. State whether h and Nu are local or mean values.

groups.label: λ²
groups.name: fin parameter squared, with λ = mL
groups.reference: L is the fin length, P the exposed perimeter and A_c the cross-sectional area.

groups.label: Q̇L/(kA_cΔT)
groups.name: base heat flow in dimensionless form
groups.reference: ΔT = T_b − T_∞ is the base excess temperature and must not be 0.

groups.label: PL/A_c
groups.name: ratio of perimeter times length to cross-sectional area
groups.reference: A geometry ratio of the fin.

groups.label: A_c/L²
groups.name: ratio of cross-sectional area to length squared
groups.reference: A geometry ratio of the fin.

groups.label: Bi
groups.name: Biot number
groups.reference: Bi needs the Biot length L_c and the solid conductivity k_s. L_c = V/A_s is the half-thickness of a slab cooled on both faces, r/2 for a long cylinder and r/3 for a sphere. A spatial solution uses the half-thickness or the radius.

groups.label: θ
groups.name: normalized temperature
groups.reference: The two differences must share one reference temperature, such as T_∞. The reference difference must not be 0.

groups.label: X
groups.name: dimensionless position
groups.reference: x is the coordinate and L the length scale of the declared domain, such as the half-thickness.

groups.label: Fo
groups.name: Fourier number
groups.reference: α_s is the solid diffusivity and L_c the same length as in Bi. When t is the time coordinate, Fo is the dimensionless time.

groups.label: Re
groups.name: Reynolds number
groups.reference: U is the reference speed and L the characteristic length. Use the same L as in Nu when an identity combines them.

groups.label: Pr
groups.name: Prandtl number
groups.reference: Pr is a ratio of fluid properties. Take all properties at one reference temperature.

groups.label: Pe
groups.name: Péclet number
groups.reference: Pe = Re Pr only when Re and Pr use the same reference properties.

groups.label: St_h
groups.name: Stanton number
groups.reference: State whether h and St_h are local or mean values.

groups.label: Gr
groups.name: Grashof number
groups.reference: State whether ΔT is a positive scale or a signed difference.

groups.label: Ra
groups.name: Rayleigh number
groups.reference: Ra = Gr Pr only when both use the same reference properties.

groups.label: Ri
groups.name: bulk Richardson number
groups.reference: A bulk Richardson number. The gradient Richardson number is a different quantity.

groups.label: Ste
groups.name: Stefan number
groups.reference: State the phase of c_p and the temperature interval of ΔT.

groups.label: Ec
groups.name: Eckert number
groups.reference: ΔT is a positive scale.

groups.label: Br
groups.name: Brinkman number
groups.reference: Br = Pr Ec only when both use the same reference properties.

groups.label: Ma_T
groups.name: thermal Marangoni number
groups.reference: Ma_T is a positive magnitude. Keep the sign of dγ/dT separately.

groups.label: NTU
groups.name: number of transfer units
groups.reference: U_HX is the overall heat-transfer coefficient, not a speed.

groups.label: C_r
groups.name: capacity rate ratio
groups.reference: C = ṁ c_p for each stream.

groups.label: τ_opt
groups.name: optical thickness
groups.reference: κ_a is the absorption coefficient of the medium.

catalogue.about: The declared model catalogue of spec section 10, one entry for each declared model of the families built so far. Each entry has the six parts that section 10 requires: model (equations, closures, geometry, conditions and the declared dimensionless form), domain (parameters and assumptions), operations (symbolic and numerical), methods (the four analyses, each with the reason it applies or not) with limitations, acceptance (standard example, reference and tolerance) and solver (method, discretization, convergence and reproducibility). A record names its declared model in purpose.declaration; the page checks the Nondimensionalizer's result against the declared dimensionless form exactly.

declarations.title: Lumped body with convection

model.summary: A body whose temperature stays uniform, with heat capacity ρc_pV, cooled through its surface A_s by convection to a fluid at T_∞.

roles.meaning: conductivity of the body, for the Biot number

closures: Newton's law of cooling with constant h: the heat flow out of the surface is hA_s(T − T_∞).
model.geometry: Any shape. The Biot length is L_c = V/A_s. The comparison with a spatial model uses the shape in the record's geometry: a slab, a long cylinder, a sphere or a cube (the product of three slab solutions).

assumptions.text: The temperature is uniform in the body at each time. The comparison with the spatial model tests this assumption.
ρ, c_p, h and T_∞ are constant.
T_i is not equal to T_∞.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_τ = −θ and θ(0) = 1 with τ = t/(ρc_pV/(hA_s)).
The exact solution θ = e^{−τ} and the exact energy balance ρc_pV(T_i − T) = ∫ hA_s(T − T_∞) dt.
The lumped model as the leading order of the small-Bi expansion of the spatial model (src/asymptotic.js).
numerical: The error of the lumped model against the spatial model of the declared shape, at each point of the map.
The decay time ρc_pV/(hA_s) and the temperature at the record's time.

dominant-balance.reason: The uniform-temperature assumption is a balance: the internal temperature drop is small compared with the drop across the surface film when Bi_c is small.

asymptotic.reason: The lumped model is the leading order of the outer expansion of the spatial model as Bi → 0 with the slow time fixed: a coupled limit.

stability.reason: The model is linear with one steady state θ = 0, and θ = e^{−τ} decays. A stability analysis adds nothing.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: The spatial comparison covers a slab, a long cylinder, a sphere and a cube. Other shapes need a separate declaration of the spatial model.
Radiation exchange makes the model nonlinear: piece 4 declares the lumped body with radiation.

acceptance.reference: θ = e^{−τ} (exact), the decay time ρc_pV/(hA_s) from the record's values (exact), and the lumped error against the mpmath slab series at Bi = 0.1.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the decay time. 1e-9 for the comparison with the series.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and condition equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The decay time from the record's values is exact, and θ(τ = 1) = e^{−1}.
The lumped error against the spatial model goes to 0 as Bi_c goes to 0 at a fixed Bi_c·Fo_c.

solver.method: Closed form θ = e^{−τ}. The spatial comparison uses the series of the declared shape (transient conduction declarations).
solver.discretization: None for the lumped model. The comparison uses 21 points in X for the slab, the cylinder and the sphere, and 21 × 21 × 21 points for the cube's symmetric octant.
solver.convergence: The same mode count rule as the transient conduction declarations: λ_n²τ ≤ 50.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision. Exact rationals for the decay time.

declarations.title: Transient conduction in a slab with surface convection

model.summary: A slab of half-thickness L with constant properties, uniform initial temperature T_i and convection to a fluid at T_∞ on its surface.
closures: Fourier's law with constant k is inside the equation: q = −k ∂T/∂x.
model.geometry: A slab of half-thickness L, symmetric about its centre plane x = 0. Both faces see the same fluid.

conditions.meaning: convection to the fluid (Newton's law of cooling)

assumptions.text: The density, the specific heat capacity and the conductivity are constant.
h and T_∞ are constant and the same on all of the surface.
The initial temperature is uniform, and T_i is not equal to T_∞.
Heat flows in x only: the slab is wide compared with its thickness.
There is no heat source in the solid, and radiation is part of h or absent.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared dimensionless equation and conditions (canonical forms).
The small-Bi outer expansion to order 3 in exact rationals, with the solvability condition and the matching constant of each order.
Exact checks of the expansion: each order satisfies its equation, its surface condition and its solvability condition.
numerical: The exact series of modes cos(λX) with eigenvalues from Brent's method.
The one-mode, lumped, first-order outer, surface-temperature and short-time approximations, and their error at each point of the map.
The energy balance d(mean θ)/dτ = −(j + 1) Bi θ(1, τ) at the inspected point.

dominant-balance.reason: The surface condition compares conduction inside the solid with exchange at the surface (Bi), and the equation compares the penetration depth with the size of the solid (Fo).

asymptotic.reason: Bi → 0 at fixed Bi·Fo gives the lumped model as the leading order of a regular outer expansion with an initial layer. Bi → ∞ gives the surface-temperature model, and Fo → 0 gives an inner region at the surface.

stability.reason: The model is linear with a unique steady state θ = 0. Each mode decays at the rate λ_n², so a stability analysis adds nothing.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so it has one solution for each Bi. No branch can split.

limitations: Constant properties only. A conductivity that changes with temperature needs a separate declaration.
Uniform h and T_∞. A surface condition that changes along the surface needs a 2D or 3D declaration.

The map uses the declared domain 0.001 ≤ Bi ≤ 1000 and 0.001 ≤ Fo ≤ 10. Where the series needs more than 400 modes, or the temperature excess is below 10⁻¹² of its initial value, the page shows an unresolved region.

acceptance.reference: The first eigenvalues and coefficients, and θ at the centre and the surface at Fo = 0.01, 0.1, 0.5 and 2 for Bi = 0.1, 1 and 10, from mpmath with 30 digits (tools/references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-9 relative for the eigenvalues and coefficients, 1e-9 absolute for θ.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The eigenvalues, coefficients and temperatures agree with the mpmath reference within the tolerance.
The series gives θ = 1 inside the solid at the earliest time of the map, within 1e-9 at X ≤ 0.5.
The small-Bi expansion gives C₁ and λ₁² to order 3 exactly as SymPy's series of the eigenvalue equation.
The energy balance holds at the example's point within 1e-9.

solver.method: Separation of variables: θ = Σ C_n f_n(λ_nX) exp(−λ_n²τ).
solver.discretization: No mesh. The error measures use 21 equally spaced points X = 0, 0.05, …, 1.
solver.convergence: The series keeps the modes with λ_n²τ ≤ 50, so the first mode left out is below e⁻⁵⁰ times its coefficient. At most 400 modes. Each eigenvalue has its own bracket, and Brent's method stops at 1e-15.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision. The same inputs give the same numbers on every run. Reference values: mpmath 1.3.0 with 30 digits.

model.summary: A long cylinder of radius R with constant properties, uniform initial temperature T_i and convection to a fluid at T_∞ on its surface.
closures: Fourier's law with constant k is inside the equation: q = −k ∂T/∂r.
model.geometry: A long solid cylinder of radius R. The temperature depends on r and t only, so the ends have no effect.

conditions.meaning: a finite temperature at the centre
convection to the fluid (Newton's law of cooling)

assumptions.text: The density, the specific heat capacity and the conductivity are constant.
h and T_∞ are constant and the same on all of the surface.
The initial temperature is uniform, and T_i is not equal to T_∞.
Heat flows in r only: the cylinder is long compared with its radius, so the ends have no effect.
There is no heat source in the solid, and radiation is part of h or absent.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared dimensionless equation and conditions (canonical forms).
The small-Bi outer expansion to order 3 in exact rationals, with the solvability condition and the matching constant of each order.
Exact checks of the expansion: each order satisfies its equation, its surface condition and its solvability condition.
numerical: The exact series of modes J₀(λX) with eigenvalues from Brent's method.
The one-mode, lumped, first-order outer, surface-temperature and short-time approximations, and their error at each point of the map.
The energy balance d(mean θ)/dτ = −(j + 1) Bi θ(1, τ) at the inspected point.

dominant-balance.reason: The surface condition compares conduction inside the solid with exchange at the surface (Bi), and the equation compares the penetration depth with the size of the solid (Fo).

asymptotic.reason: Bi → 0 at fixed Bi·Fo gives the lumped model as the leading order of a regular outer expansion with an initial layer. Bi → ∞ gives the surface-temperature model, and Fo → 0 gives an inner region at the surface.

stability.reason: The model is linear with a unique steady state θ = 0. Each mode decays at the rate λ_n², so a stability analysis adds nothing.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so it has one solution for each Bi. No branch can split.

limitations: Constant properties only. A conductivity that changes with temperature needs a separate declaration.

declarations.title: Transient conduction in a sphere with surface convection

model.summary: A sphere of radius R with constant properties, uniform initial temperature T_i and convection to a fluid at T_∞ on its surface.
closures: Fourier's law with constant k is inside the equation: q = −k ∂T/∂r.
model.geometry: A solid sphere of radius R. The temperature depends on r and t only.

conditions.meaning: a finite temperature at the centre
convection to the fluid (Newton's law of cooling)

assumptions.text: The density, the specific heat capacity and the conductivity are constant.
h and T_∞ are constant and the same on all of the surface.
The initial temperature is uniform, and T_i is not equal to T_∞.
Heat flows in r only: the surface condition is the same at every point.
There is no heat source in the solid, and radiation is part of h or absent.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared dimensionless equation and conditions (canonical forms).
The small-Bi outer expansion to order 3 in exact rationals, with the solvability condition and the matching constant of each order.

numerical: The exact series of modes sin(λX)/(λX) with eigenvalues from Brent's method.
The one-mode, lumped, first-order outer, surface-temperature and short-time approximations, and their error at each point of the map.
The energy balance d(mean θ)/dτ = −(j + 1) Bi θ(1, τ) at the inspected point.

dominant-balance.reason: The surface condition compares conduction inside the solid with exchange at the surface (Bi), and the equation compares the penetration depth with the size of the solid (Fo).

asymptotic.reason: Bi → 0 at fixed Bi·Fo gives the lumped model as the leading order of a regular outer expansion with an initial layer. Bi → ∞ gives the surface-temperature model, and Fo → 0 gives an inner region at the surface.

stability.reason: The model is linear with a unique steady state θ = 0. Each mode decays at the rate λ_n², so a stability analysis adds nothing.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so it has one solution for each Bi. No branch can split.

limitations: Constant properties only. A conductivity that changes with temperature needs a separate declaration.

declarations.title: Slab with a uniform heat source, steady state

model.summary: A slab of half-thickness L with a uniform volumetric heat source q_v, cooled by convection on both faces. Steady state, constant properties.

roles.meaning: reference temperature difference, such as the allowed rise

model.geometry: A slab of half-thickness L, symmetric about x = 0, with the same fluid on both faces.

assumptions.text: The source q_v, the conductivity, h and T_∞ are constant.
The slab is at steady state.
ΔT is a positive reference scale, such as the allowed temperature rise.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_XX + Γ = 0 with the declared conditions.
The exact solution θ = Γ(1 − X²)/2 + Γ/Bi in rationals, the heat balance Γ = Bi θ(1), and the exact approximation boundaries.
numerical: None: every value is an exact rational when the inputs are rational.

dominant-balance.reason: The internal temperature drop Γ/2 and the surface excess Γ/Bi compete. Their ratio is Bi/2 exactly.

asymptotic.reason: Bi → 0 gives a uniform temperature and Bi → ∞ gives a prescribed surface temperature. Each expansion stops after two terms, so each two-term result is exact.

stability.reason: The steady linear model has one solution. A stability analysis needs the transient model and adds nothing for a constant source.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: Steady state only. The declaration of the transient slab gives the time history without a source.
A source that depends on temperature, such as a reaction, makes the model nonlinear and needs a separate declaration.

acceptance.reference: θ = Γ(1 − X²)/2 + Γ/Bi (exact, in rationals) and its heat balance. SymPy solves the same boundary-value problem (tools/references.py).
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The solution satisfies the equation and both conditions exactly, and SymPy gives the same polynomial.
The heat balance: the source Γ leaves through the surface as Bi θ(1) (exact).
The balance crossover is at Bi = 2 exactly.

solver.convergence: None needed: the solution is exact.
solver.reproducibility: Exact rationals give the same digits on every machine.

declarations.title: Two-layer plane wall with a contact resistance

model.summary: Two plane layers in series with a thermal contact resistance R_c between them, convection to a fluid on each face, steady state.
closures: Fourier's law with a constant conductivity in each layer.
The contact resistance: the heat flux across the interface is (T_1 − T_2)/R_c.
model.geometry: Layer 1 on 0 < x < L_1 and layer 2 on L_1 < x < L_1 + L_2. Face 1 is at x = 0 and face 2 at x = L_1 + L_2.

conditions.meaning: the temperature jump across the contact resistance

parameters.meaning: contact resistance in units of the resistance of layer 1
Biot number of face 2, with L_1 and k_1

assumptions.text: Steady state and constant properties in each layer.
Heat flows in x only: the wall is wide compared with its thickness.
The thermal contact resistance R_c is a declared input per unit area. It is not a mechanical contact model.
T_∞1 is not equal to T_∞2.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared equations and the four conditions.
The exact solution in rationals: the series resistances, the heat flux, every interface temperature and the jump across the contact.
Exact checks: the heat flux is the same in each layer and through the contact, and the temperatures close at fluid 2.
The resistance limits r_c → 0 (perfect contact) and r_c → ∞ (no heat flow), with exact error formulas.
numerical: The map evaluates the exact formulas in double precision.

dominant-balance.reason: The temperature drop across each element is the heat flux times its resistance, so the largest resistance controls the heat flow.

asymptotic.reason: r_c → 0 and r_c → ∞ are regular limits of the exact solution, with a convergent series in r_c divided by the other resistances.

stability.reason: The steady linear model has one solution.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: Two layers in the record match. The resistance network works for more layers, but the record match covers two.
Mechanical contact (pressure, roughness) needs a separate structural declaration. R_c is an input here.

acceptance.reference: The resistance sum, heat flux and interface temperatures in exact rationals, and SymPy's solution of the same linear system (tools/references.py).
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equations and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The heat flux is the same in each layer and through the contact (exact).
The temperature jump across the contact is q R_c (exact), and the temperatures close at fluid 2 (exact).
SymPy's solution of the linear system gives the same heat flux and temperatures.

solver.method: Series thermal resistances in exact rationals.
solver.reproducibility: Exact rationals give the same digits on every machine.

declarations.title: Straight fin of constant cross-section

model.summary: A straight fin of length L, cross-section A_c and exposed perimeter P, with uniform convection h, a prescribed base temperature and an insulated or convective tip.
closures: Fourier's law along the fin with constant k, and Newton's law of cooling on the sides with constant h.
model.geometry: A straight fin with constant A_c and P. x runs from the base (x = 0) to the tip (x = L).

alternatives.meaning: a convective tip with the same h

parameters.meaning: fin parameter mL, with m² = hP/(kA_c)
tip Biot number hL/k (0 for an insulated tip)

assumptions.text: Constant conductivity, uniform h and a prescribed base temperature.
The temperature varies along x only. The transverse validity condition needs its own derivation, which the dominant-balance step gives.
ΔT = T_b − T_∞ is not 0.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_XX − λ²θ = 0, θ(0) = 1 and the tip condition.
The small-λ expansion to order λ⁸ in exact rationals, with each order checked against its equation and conditions.
The large-λ boundary layer at the base and its matching to the outer solution θ = 0.
numerical: θ(X) = cosh(λ(1 − X))/cosh λ for the insulated tip, Q̇L/(kA_cΔT) = λ tanh λ and η_f = tanh λ/λ, written with e^{−λ} so that no value overflows.
The base heat flow against the total heat loss of the surface, by Gauss–Legendre quadrature.

dominant-balance.reason: Conduction along the fin and loss through the surface compete through λ². Conduction across the fin and loss at the surface compete through the transverse Biot number hA_c/(kP).

asymptotic.reason: λ → 0 is a regular expansion in λ². λ → ∞ loses the second derivative in the outer region, so a boundary layer of thickness 1/λ forms at the base.

stability.reason: The steady linear model has one solution.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: Constant cross-section only. A tapered or annular fin needs a separate declaration.
The 1D model does not establish the transverse condition hA_c/(kP) ≪ 1. The page shows that estimate as a separate balance.

acceptance.reference: λ tanh λ, tanh λ/λ and the profile at λ = √(11/32) from mpmath with 30 digits, and the Taylor series of λ tanh λ from SymPy (tools/references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-12 relative for the heat flow and the profile. Exact for the series coefficients.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The base heat flow, the efficiency and the profile agree with mpmath within the tolerance.
The base heat flow equals the total heat loss of the surface within 1e-12.
The small-λ expansion gives the Taylor coefficients of λ tanh λ exactly.

solver.method: Closed form with exponentials: θ = [(1 + β)e^{−λX} + (1 − β)e^{−λ(2 − X)}]/[(1 + β) + (1 − β)e^{−2λ}], β = Bi_t/λ.
solver.discretization: None. The heat-balance check uses 8 panels of the 20-point Gauss–Legendre rule.
solver.convergence: None needed for the closed form.

references.about: Reference values from SymPy's exact rational matrices, independent of the page's engine. Written by tools/references.py; CI compares the engine with this file and never runs the script.

settings.roots: mpmath.findroot(anderson) in the bracket of each mode
settings.coefficients: mpmath.quad of the weighted mode integrals
